title: Jonah and the Radiators
premise: Kestrel Iversen, a bridge inspector whose marriage is measured in millimeters of drift, hears a song on the radio that their late mother wrote and never recorded — a song only one other living person could know. The broadcast pulls Kestrel back to the failing radiator factory town of Jonah's Bend, where the family's inheritance, an old betrayal, and the truth about who really wrote the songs all wait. As Kestrel and their spouse Wren unravel the mystery of the unrecorded catalog, they must decide whether protecting the family myth is worth losing each other. In the end, Kestrel chooses truth over loyalty, plays the song publicly in the town square, and lets the marriage — like the bridge — be rebuilt on honest load-bearing terms.
about_author: Dominic Eastwick is the pen name of a former structural engineer who spent eleven years inspecting truss bridges across the upper Midwest before turning to fiction. Their work examines how families, like bridges, fail slowly and then suddenly.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. On a routine inspection of the Corliss Street Bridge, Kestrel measures gaps with calipers while mentally measuring the distance to Wren at breakfast. Emotional beat: quiet dread disguised as competence.

chapters.title: The Song That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Driving home, a radio station plays 'Radiator Hymn' — a song Kestrel watched their mother write and deliberately never record. They pull over, shaking. Beat: the past arrives uninvited.

chapters.title: Wren at the Window
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren watches Kestrel come home without explaining where they've been, recognizing the old silence returning. A dinner of almost-conversations. Beat: love strained by withheld truth.

chapters.title: Jonah's Bend, Population Falling
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel calls their uncle Ambrose, who confirms someone has been shopping the mother's unreleased tapes. Kestrel decides to go back; Wren insists on coming. Beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: The House on Foundry Road
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The childhood home is half-cleared for sale by cousin Delia, who greets them with suspicion and a lawyer's card. Boxes of unlabeled cassettes everywhere. Beat: inheritance as battlefield.

chapters.title: Delia's Ledger
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia reveals she's been managing the estate and resents Kestrel's five-year absence. She hints the tapes are worth more than sentiment. Beat: resentment wearing the mask of duty.

chapters.title: Ambrose in the Basement
chapters.summary: Ambrose's POV. Uncle Ambrose, former studio engineer, shows Kestrel the reel-to-reel machine and admits he made copies years ago — but swears he never sold one. Beat: guilt surfacing after decades.

chapters.title: What Wren Heard
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren secretly listens to a cassette and hears not just the music but a second voice — a man singing harmony no one ever mentioned. Beat: discovery that reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Harmony Voice
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel confronts Ambrose about the male voice; he goes pale and says only, 'Ask about Ray.' Beat: the family myth cracks open.

chapters.title: Ray Ostrander's Garage
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel finds Ray Ostrander, a dying former radiator-factory welder, living above his garage. He recognizes Kestrel instantly — 'You have her chin.' Beat: meeting the ghost in the flesh.

chapters.title: Five Years of Almost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. While Kestrel spends days with Ray, Wren wanders Jonah's Bend, interviewing old factory workers, realizing how much of Kestrel's life was built on omission. Beat: loneliness inside companionship.

chapters.title: The Co-Writer Nobody Named
chapters.summary: Ray's POV. Ray explains he co-wrote every song with Kestrel's mother, Marion, in the factory lunchroom — and that her husband, Kestrel's father, erased him from every credit. Beat: stolen legacy revealed.

chapters.title: Marion's Rule
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Flashback chapter: young Kestrel overhears Marion refusing to record because 'if it's recorded, it belongs to him.' Kestrel realizes the silence was protection. Beat: grief recontextualized.

chapters.title: Delia Makes Her Move
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia signs a deal with a Nashville licensing firm for the tapes, claiming sole authority as estate executor. Beat: ambition outrunning honesty.

chapters.title: The Contract on the Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads Delia's contract and spots that it credits all songs solely to Marion's estate — erasing Ray again. Wren must decide whether to tell Kestrel or protect the fragile peace. Beat: loyalty vs. truth, mirrored.

chapters.title: Wren Speaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tells Kestrel about the contract's credit clause — and about the five years of things Kestrel hasn't said. First real fight. Beat: rupture as beginning.

chapters.title: Calipers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel, devastated, measures the gap between what they feel and what they say, admitting to themselves they learned silence from Marion. Beat: self-recognition.

chapters.title: Ray's Last Verse
chapters.summary: Ray's POV. Ray, weakening, gives Kestrel a notebook: forty years of lyrics in two handwritings, interleaved. Proof. Beat: inheritance redefined as evidence and love.

chapters.title: Delia's Defense
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia reveals her motive: debts from keeping the house and Ambrose's care afloat. The deal wasn't greed; it was survival. Beat: antagonist becomes human.

chapters.title: The Radio Station
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel traces the broadcast to a low-power community station run by a young DJ, Priya, who bought the tape at an estate sale. Beat: the leak found, the stakes clarified.

chapters.title: Priya's Tape
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya refuses to name her buyer but shows the tape's label: Ambrose's handwriting. Beat: betrayal from within the family.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Reel-to-Reel
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel confronts Ambrose, who confesses he sold copies to pay medical bills and believed the songs deserved to outlive the lie. Beat: anger giving way to terrible understanding.

chapters.title: What the Father Knew
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Digging through the father's papers, Kestrel finds letters proving he knew about Ray all along and threatened Marion with exposure if she credited him. Beat: the true villain named posthumously.

chapters.title: Marion's Letter, Unsent
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds an unsent letter from Marion to Ray, apologizing and asking him to forgive her silence. She gives it to Kestrel instead of reading it alone. Beat: intimacy through shared grief.

chapters.title: Ray Listens
chapters.summary: Ray's POV. Kestrel reads Marion's letter aloud to Ray. He weeps, then asks one thing: to hear the songs played right, once, with his name said. Beat: a dying wish becomes the mission.

chapters.title: Delia Rethinks
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Shown the notebook and the letters, Delia stalls the Nashville deal, risking her own finances. Beat: costly integrity.

chapters.title: The Bridge Inspection
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Back on the Corliss Bridge, Kestrel finds a critical crack and halts traffic — the first time they've refused to let something deteriorate quietly. Beat: professional act mirrors personal turn.

chapters.title: Wren's Ultimatum, Softened
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tells Kestrel they'll stay — but only if Kestrel stops practicing almost-saying-it, starting now, starting with everything. Beat: conditional grace.

chapters.title: Everything, Then
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel tells Wren everything: the overheard vow, the shame, the fear of becoming their father. Long night, no resolution, but no more hiding. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Permits and Permission
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya offers the station for a live broadcast of the songs; Delia secures Ray's consent as co-author in writing. Beat: allies assemble.

chapters.title: Objections
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Marion's old label threatens litigation over the catalog. Delia, holding the notebook, refuses to fold. Beat: external pressure peaks.

chapters.title: Ray Fails
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ray is hospitalized; doctors give him days. The broadcast may not happen in time. Beat: clock running down.

chapters.title: Hospital Harmonies
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, a lapsed choir singer, learns the harmonies from the tapes at Ray's bedside so the songs can be sung properly. Beat: Wren claims a place in the story.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel rehearses alone in the empty house, playing Marion's guitar badly, speaking to her ghost. Beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Broadcast from Jonah's Bend
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Live on Priya's station: Kestrel narrates the true history, Wren sings, Delia reads from the notebook, and Ray's name is spoken into the record. Beat: climax — truth performed publicly.

chapters.title: Ray Hears It
chapters.summary: Ray's POV. From his hospital bed, Ray listens to the broadcast, hears his own words sung back to him, and lets go peacefully that night. Beat: release.

chapters.title: Aftermath and Accusations
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. The label backs down under public pressure; royalties are structured to honor both writers. Delia and Kestrel reach an uneasy, real peace. Beat: justice without triumphalism.

chapters.title: The Estate Settled
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The house sells; Kestrel keeps only the notebook and the reel-to-reel. Ambrose, forgiven but not excused, moves near Delia. Beat: inheritance distributed honestly.

chapters.title: Load Rating
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren and Kestrel walk the repaired Corliss Bridge together, talking plainly about what comes next — therapy, maybe a move, maybe staying. Beat: the marriage re-rated for honest loads.

chapters.title: Radiator Hymn (Reprise)
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. One year later, Kestrel plays 'Radiator Hymn' on the radio for Priya's anniversary show, dedicating it to Marion, Ray, and Wren — saying all of it, finally, out loud. Beat: resolution; the song, once silenced, endures.
